side_b: manifests/family_model.json moderation:{allegation_type} body "moderation subject digest required (moderation_subject_digest)"
note: CC 2.1, CC 2.6.1.2 and CC 2.6.1.7 each give `subject_sha256_ed25519_raw` as optional on a `moderation:*` row (absent: "the subject is named some other way, or not at all"). The body cell, read from the shipped store, says the digest is required. A moderation row with no digest is admitted under the text and refused under the cell. If the cell only means "well-formed when present" it should say so.

side_a: CC 3.1.3 id = sha256(domain ‖ JCS(object)); a receiver re-derives the row and refuses any byte difference
note: CC 3.1.3 gives the minted identity:occurrence_revocation row, and the cosign:signature row, an id that is a SHA-256; the table and CDDL type attestation_id as a 36-character UUID and the gate refuses an ill-typed member. How 32 digest bytes become the UUID is nowhere stated, and the receiver refuses any byte difference, so two mints of one object can refuse each other

side_a: CC 4.5.5 A duty action (`takedown_notice`, `moderation:*`, `reconsideration:*`, `slashing:*`, `quarantine:*`) is admitted **iff** one holds **positively**
side_b: manifests/family_model.json slashing:{outcome} signer_rule (code-v61): who any_registered, via none; transitions.json attest roles: registered
note: The text puts slashing verdicts under the enforced duty-holder gate with scope slash (CC 4.5.5 scope table, CC 4.4.3.4.3); quarantine's cell carries seat_role(slash) but slashing's cell admits anyone. C068 settled the text side only.

side_a: CC 3.2 The age band is the I1 band (`age_self_declared` / `age_assurance:*`, [CC 3.3.12](part_3_the_namespace.md); `minor` < 18 / `adult` ≥ 18).
side_b: CC 3.4.13 The guardian MUST be ≥ `age_assurance:provider:adult` as a floor, and the guardianship relationship to that specific child MUST be verified.
note: The CC 3.2 admission predicate for a guardian's binding asks only age_band(S) == adult on the I1 band, which a self-declaration supplies; CC 3.4.13 asks a provider-rung assurance and a verified relationship. One admits a self-declared adult as guardian, the other refuses. CC 3.4.13 is the minors' home.

side_a: CC 3.1.4: "each period's row `supersedes` the previous one in the same lineage, and a row is purgeable after `valid_until`"
note: CC 3.1.4 and CC 5.4.6 item 6 sign each period's row with a fresh rendezvous key (attester = subject = the period's key), yet have it supersede the previous period's row. The data (and the CC 8.10 card: supersede by author) admit a supersede only from the same attester, as CC 2.4.1 defines the verb, so the next hour's row cannot supersede. Expiry at valid_until does the work in practice; the supersedes clause cannot be followed.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.3: "**`federation` for Commons and `public` content**. The substrate refuses a report whose scope is not its content's."
side_b: CC 5.2: "the only plaintext bodies are those of authorized infrastructure communities and public rooms, which"
note: CC 5.2 and CC 1.13.3.4 put an authorized infrastructure community's holding claims at federation scope with the public room's; CC 3.1.3.3 rule (1) names only Commons and public content for federation and refuses any other report whose scope is not its content's (`community`). A reader of rule (1) refuses the infrastructure community's federation-scope custody report that a reader of CC 5.2 emits. CC 4.4.3.2.1 (plaintext by the record) supports CC 5.2.

side_a: CC 3.2: "there is no member-level listing, and a roster is never enumerable outside its cohort, a public room's included"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json membership:{stage} replication.audience note: "may_receive_group_plane (public group: everyone; private: members' nodes, live invitees, named member); proposal: addressee (invitee)"
note: CC 3.2 and the CC 5.2 audience table (public room: an outsider learns the listing, the holding claims and the content, "never the roster") keep a public room's membership rows inside its roster; the model cell serves a public group's membership rows to everyone, which makes the roster enumerable by any node.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.7: "a Goal is amended by `supersedes`, retired by `withdraws`, and disowned by `recants`"
note: The text gives a Goal's declarer `recants`; the model's verb cell (source cc-table) and the transitions omit it, though the cell's own code reading records "+recant". A door built from the data refuses the recant the text admits. approach:{goal_id} carries recant; goal does not.

side_a: CC 3.1.3: "**Yes — the accord holders, cosigned at the charter's M**; never a single holder, never the node itself"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json transport:canonical_rebind supersede: roles "author", policy "selfAct"
note: The attest transition now carries the cosigned accord policy (C369, C374 fixed there), but the supersede transition beside it is still one-signer: the holder who authored a re-bind replaces it alone, which is a re-bind by a single holder. The CC 8.10 card shows the same line.

side_a: CC 4.5.13: A lift undoes what can be undone: a warning, a block for the room, a withhold, and a takedown still inside its withhold window
side_b: CC 4.5.3: They are withheld while an admitted notice stands against them with no admitted reversal.
note: CC 4.5.3 computes withholding from one reversal only, a review-holder's `reconsideration` row with outcome `reversed`; CC 4.5.13 adds the members' lift by objection rows. A holder built from CC 4.5.3 keeps withholding after a lift and deletes at the window; the lift paragraph is the later and more specific

side_a: CC 1.13.2: A person may stop, remove, or eject an agent from their own device, their own life, or a community they moderate, at any time and for any reason
side_b: CC 4.5.13: So no single key, a moderator's or a founder's, removes a member alone
note: CC 1.13.2 gives a moderator alone the ejection of an agent from the community and calls it a moderation act; CC 4.5.13 says a single signature never removes from the roster. Where an agent's key is on a roster the two differ; CC 4.5.13 states no exception for agents and CC 1.13.2 calls its rule one no finding moves

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.3: **Pinned `infra:*` one-liners (closed set).** Each token has one pinned meaning:
note: the text closes the `infra:*` set at eight tokens, matched as exact strings, and allows only a family sub-scope of `infra:attest`; the family model gates detector, assurance and hard-case rows on three tokens outside the set (C423 touches one of them). A delegation written from the text carries `infra:attest` and fails the data's door

side_a: CC 3.2: For a **removal**, every member other than the target signs *and* those signers are a strict majority of the roster
side_b: data constitution/governance_policy.tsv: community_remove enact "2/3", base "active", kind two_path, reverse_path no
note: which count removes a member: the room's declared `consensus_protocol` (all others under `unanimous`, a strict majority under `majority`) or the policy row's two thirds of the expected-active base. The same question as C283 for admission, which is open with the steward; the removal side is not listed there

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.5: "so the first write after the removal is under a key the removed member was never granted"
side_b: CC 5.1: "A removed member's exposure window is therefore `≤ T`, never "until the next scheduled rotation"."
note: 4.4.3.4.5 (the one statement of the removal rule, 'at any scope') gives a removed member nothing new; 5.1 MUST coalesce removals into one rotation per window T (2 s) and lets writes inside T seal under the old epoch. 4.4.3.2.1 makes the community DEK the 5.1 cascade, so the two instants meet on one key. 4.4.3.2.2 and 1.13.3.3 support rotate-before-next-write.

side_b: CC 4.4.3.5.2: "return # no SLA commitment; no watcher"
note: With no deletion commitment on a producer's row, CC 2.1 gives it a default window (so a deadline and a breach exist) and CC 4.4.3.5.2 runs no watcher at all. No default window is stated anywhere, and reactions.json starts the clock only from a `consent:deletion_sla:{days}` row. The watcher also reads the row only: a row carrying the `deletion_window` member and no `deletion_sla` row is watched under CC 3.3.1 ('the member carries the commitment') and not under 4.4.3.5.2.

side_a: CC 3.2: The acceptance edge is a person's row: any live key of the person's roster signs it as that person
note: trust:{job}:{version} signer_rule (code-v61) has the node sign its own acceptance edge to the root; CC 3.2 T3 and CC 4.4.3.8 make the edge the owner's (owner to root), read by every node and agent the person owns, a node's own edge read only while the owner has signed none. One deletion un-trusts every node only under the text. The text (3.1.1 row, 3.2, 4.4.3.8) agrees with itself.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: "A node MUST admit a `withdraws` against a target row `T` when one line of this table holds. It MUST refuse any other with `federation_withdraws_not_admitted`."
side_b: CC 7.5.5: "the key named in `decided_by` withdraws the `decided` row, admitted because that row names it (the lineage-witness rule, as for the custodian)"
note: The admission table has five lines (quorum, signer, a key in subject_key_ids, hash proxy, delegate). A key named in the envelope member decided_by is none of them, so a node built from CC 2.4.1.1 refuses the decider's cancellation that CC 7.5.5 and CC 3.1.5 admit, unless decided_by is also in subject_key_ids, which no section says. The retirement model assumes the CC 7.5.5 reading.

side_a: CC 2.4: "so no single signer and no subject can retire a community, un-name a charter or retract a roster event"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: trust:{job}:{version} withdraw admitted withdrawn author,subject selfAct
note: trust:{job}:{version} withdraw is selfAct by author or subject for every job. A trust:charter row that carries a scrub set (the keyless family root, the witness quorum the cosign_rule cell names) is a cosigned row, and rule 0 lets only the quorum withdraw it. The data does not separate the cosigned charter from the single-signer confers and accepts edges.

reactions.json has two expiry entries for consent:state:{stance} leaf granted, both optional on valid_until: one with no default (cites CC 3.3.1, 4.4.3.5.5) and one with default consent_temporary_ttl_secs counted from asserted_at (cites CC 4.4.3.5.6). The text lapses only a grant that carries a valid_until; 14 days is the TEMPORARY bundle's, and constants.tsv says so ("for a temporary grant that states no `valid_until`"). The second entry has no condition naming the temporary stream, so a kernel reading it lapses every undated grant at 14 days.
